 Three years since conviction

 Five years since conviction

Tier B: misdemeanors, or misdemeanors combined with violations, in the same case 
 Five years since conviction

Tier B: the six listed felonies 
 Ten years since conviction or release from incarceration, whichever is later

entries: The petitioner signs and verifies the Request. A wet signature is expected.

Section 5.2(d)(1) requires filing with the clerk of the court where the arrests occurred or the charges were brought, not the county of residence. A separate petition is filed in each county involved. Cook County filings go to the district matching the case.

clerk 
 Circuit clerk of the county of arrest or charge 
 File with the circuit clerk in each county where an arrest occurred or a charge was brought. The clerk performs service under § 5.2(d)(4).

File the Request, Case List, any Additional Cases forms and the proposed Order with the circuit clerk in each county where an arrest occurred or a charge was brought. E-file where the county requires it. AOIC requires the PDF to be flattened before e-filing, so LegalEase output is delivered pre-flattened.
A circuit clerk fee plus an ISP processing fee, both county-collected.
County totals commonly run from roughly $60 to $235; McLean County publishes $136.
ISP charges nothing to file a petition and $60 to process a court order.

Judge, clerk, prosecutor and court blocks are left blank. LegalEase completes paragraphs 1 through 4 of the granting and denying orders, which recite the participant's own identity and case facts, and never drafts the findings language or paragraph 8 of the denial order, which is the court's reason.
Race, ethnicity and Social Security number

Race, ethnicity and Social Security number on the Criminal Cover Sheet and the order cover sheet are left for the participant to complete by hand, pending the data-protection review. The Criminal Cover Sheet states the Social Security number is not mandatory, is not a public record, is stored separately and is destroyed within a reasonable time.

The Certificate of Service and Mailing on the Notice of Hearing is left blank and visibly labelled for clerk completion. It reads in the first person but its signature line is "(Clerk of the Court) (Deputy Clerk)", K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(1) puts notice on the court, and the Judicial Council instructions have the participant file the original plus copies and the clerk send them. LegalEase must never prefill it or have the participant sign it.

The hearing date, time, courthouse, division and room are left blank on the Notice of Hearing. The participant obtains them from the clerk or the assigned judge's administrative assistant after filing, and writes them in. The packet generates before the court supplies them.
The petitioner signs the petition, affirming under penalty of perjury that the statements are accurate to the best of their knowledge.

Statewide statute and statewide forms, executed county by county across 31 judicial districts. K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(1) directs the petition to the convicting court. The Judicial Council instructions tell the participant to file with the clerk of the court in the county in which they were arrested. For the ordinary case these are the same county; where they differ, the statute governs and the participant confirms with the clerk.

clerk 
 Clerk of the convicting district court 
 All petitions for expungement are docketed in the original criminal action under K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(3). The Judicial Council instructions nonetheless require a Criminal Cover Sheet, whose own text says it initiates a criminal docket sheet. The court with trial jurisdiction over the offence in the parish of arrest, under Article 972.1: district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts.

clerk 
 Clerk of court for the parish of arrest 
 File the Article 989 motion with the proposed Article 991 and Article 992 orders. The clerk collects the Article 983 fees at filing unless a returned Article 988 fee exemption is appended, and thereafter serves the district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting agency under Article 979.
Article 983(A) caps the total cost of obtaining a court order of expungement at five hundred fifty dollars.

Article 983(F) waives all fees where a district attorney certification verifies no felony convictions and no pending felony charge under a bill of information or indictment, together with one of the listed non-conviction grounds — acquittal of all charges after trial including lesser and included offences, no prosecution within the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, dismissal or refusal before the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, factual innocence with entitlement to compensation under R.S.
The clerk collects at the time of filing and Article 983 makes the fees non-refundable even if the motion is denied.

Article 983(F), claimed through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption. The form goes to the district attorney before filing and comes back within fifteen days. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.

Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion.

Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date.

Arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, or a parish or municipal ordinance equivalent, where the person entered a pretrial diversion programme 
 Five years from the date of arrest for that offence (Art. 976(B)). The Article 989 form carries a dedicated check-box for it.

Every other Article 976 ground 
 None. There is no waiting period; where prosecution was never instituted the ground is the expiry of the time limitation for prosecution itself.
Any named agency files an Article 990 affidavit of response objecting to the motion.
The court sets a contradictory hearing under Article 980(D).

Article 978(A)(1) — the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 893(E) 
 None. The set-aside and dismissal is the qualifying event, and it is obtained on the separate Article 987 track.

Article 978(A)(2) — the ten-year route 
 More than ten years from completion of any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, with no conviction of ANY OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENCE during that ten-year period and no criminal charge pending. This is not the misdemeanour test with a larger number: the misdemeanour clean period bars felony convictions only, and this one bars any criminal offence.

Article 978(A)(3) — the first offender pardon route 
 None beyond entitlement to the pardon itself. Under R.S. 15:572 a first offender never previously convicted of a felony is automatically pardoned on completion of sentence without a Board of Pardons recommendation or gubernatorial action, but no pardon issues unless the court costs for the conviction are paid.

Article 978(E) — the violent-offence lane for aggravated battery, second degree battery, aggravated criminal damage to property, simple robbery, purse snatching, or illegal use of weapons or dangerous instrumentalities 
 More than ten years since completion of sentence, deferred adjudication, probation or parole, with no criminal conviction during that period and no pending charge, and only after a contradictory hearing at which the court may grant relief in its discretion.

Article 978(A)(1) — the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 893(E) 
 None. The set-aside and dismissal is the qualifying event, and it is obtained on the separate Article 987 track.

Article 978(A)(2) — the ten-year route 
 More than ten years from completion of any sentence, deferred adjudication, or period of probation or parole, with no conviction of ANY OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENCE during that ten-year period and no criminal charge pending. This is not the misdemeanour test with a larger number: the misdemeanour clean period bars felony convictions only, and this one bars any criminal offence.

Article 978(A)(3) — the first offender pardon route 
 None beyond entitlement to the pardon itself. Under R.S. 15:572 a first offender never previously convicted of a felony is automatically pardoned on completion of sentence without a Board of Pardons recommendation or gubernatorial action, but no pardon issues unless the court costs for the conviction are paid.

Article 978(E) — the violent-offence lane for aggravated battery, second degree battery, aggravated criminal damage to property, simple robbery, purse snatching, or illegal use of weapons or dangerous instrumentalities 
 More than ten years since completion of sentence, deferred adjudication, probation or parole, with no criminal conviction during that period and no pending charge, and only after a contradictory hearing at which the court may grant relief in its discretion.

 Your Mississippi Non-Conviction Expungement Packet 
 process_guidance 
 required 
 What this packet is 
 static 
 This is a five-part self-help packet for the Mississippi non-conviction pathway in Miss. Code Ann. Section 99-19-71(4). It is prepared from the facts you verified against your records. 
 Packet contents 
 contents_list 
 Records to have beside you 
 participant_checklist_summary 
 Signing and notarization 
 static 
 DO NOT SIGN THE PETITION IN ADVANCE. You must sign the Petition and its Verification in the physical presence of a notary public. Bring satisfactory identification. The notary must administer an oath or affirmation, witness the signature, complete the notarial certificate, and affix the official notary stamp. The packet is not filing-ready until those steps are complete. 
 Important limits 
 static 
 LegalEase does not file this packet and does not guarantee relief. Before filing, confirm the filing method, local form preference, fee or waiver treatment, copy count, and service practice with the records office of the court that handled the case. Stop and get legal help when a record is ambiguous or a stopping condition in the instructions applies.

Any statement that the petitioner is rehabilitated or that annulment is consistent with the public welfare
Everything in the FOR COURT USE ONLY section
Filing one petition per charge with the clerk of each disposing court
Payment of the $125.00 filing fee and the $100 Department of Corrections investigation fee, or the waiver papers instead
Route on disposition date and conviction date at the January 1, 2019 line
Sworn signature on the petition under penalties of law.
The Circuit Court District Division or Superior Court that disposed of the charge. Separate petitions for charges in different courts.

clerk 
 Clerk of the disposing court 
 Unified statewide system with no local variation identified. One petition per charge; petitions filed at the same time in one court location share a single $125.00 filing fee. The court orders a Department of Corrections investigation, which the petitioner pays for, and provides a copy of the petition to the prosecutor.
$100 Department of Corrections investigation fee under RSA 651:5, IX unless the petitioner demonstrates indigency.
$100 Department of Safety fee for a successful petitioner.
$125.00 per court location, confirmed on the current Circuit Court Filing Fees schedule and covering petitions filed at the same time in that court.
State police fee not to exceed $100 under X(d).
Whether the Department of Safety fee and the state police fee are one charge or two is recorded below.

Motion for Waiver of Filing Fee, NHJB-2311, with the Statement of Assets and Liabilities, NHJB-2328. Indigency exempts the Department of Corrections and Department of Safety fees under RSA 651:5, IX. The state police fee waiver request must be accompanied by an affidavit of the petitioner's and spouse's monthly net income and assets.

Class A felony. RSA 651:5, III(e) 
 10 years after completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence

Class A misdemeanor or felony under RSA 318-B:26, II. RSA 651:5, III(i) 
 2 years after completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence

Class A misdemeanor. RSA 651:5, III(c) 
 3 years after completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence

Class B felony. RSA 651:5, III(d) 
 5 years after completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence

Class B misdemeanor, conviction before 01/01/2019, or on or after that date where it was not the highest offense of conviction. RSA 651:5, III(b)(1) 
 2 years after completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence

Felony indecent exposure or lewdness under RSA 645:1, II. RSA 651:5, III(g) 
 10 years after completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence

Misdemeanor domestic violence under RSA 631:2-b, subject to the tail rule that a later RSA 631:2-b conviction defers the earlier one until the most recent becomes eligible. RSA 651:5, III(h) 
 10 years after completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence

Sexual assault under RSA 632-A:4. RSA 651:5, III(f) 
 10 years after completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence

Violation, conviction before 01/01/2019, or on or after that date where it was not the highest offense of conviction, unless the underlying conviction was for an offense specified under RSA 259:39. RSA 651:5, III(a)(1) 
 1 year after completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence
Paragraph VIII dismisses a non-qualifying petition without a hearing, and paragraph IV then bars a further petition for three years.

Relief is discretionary: paragraph I lets the court annul if the annulment will assist rehabilitation and be consistent with the public welfare, and the court may decide without a hearing unless the petitioner requests one.

nd-cover-and-contents 
 cover_and_contents 
 Your North Dakota Sealing Packet 
 custom_pleading 
 required 
 What this packet is 
 static 
 This packet asks the court that entered your judgment to seal the court record of a first-offense marijuana or THC possession case under North Dakota Century Code chapter 19-03.1. Under that chapter the court must seal the record on motion when the conditions are met, so this is a motion asking for something the statute requires rather than a request for the court's discretion. 
 What is in it 
 contents_list 
 What you still have to do 
 participant_checklist_summary 
 What this packet is not 
 static 
 This packet is not legal advice and it is not a filing service. It is prepared from the facts you gave and from the statute; you file it yourself. It does not use North Dakota's general sealing chapter 12-60.1, which has its own waiting periods and its own burden of proof, and it is not the Summary Pardon Application administered by the Pardon Advisory Board.

nd-legal-effect 
 legal_effect_explanation 
 What sealing does, and what it does not do 
 process_guidance 
 required 
 nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-legal-effect-explanation-3 
 What the order does 
 static 
 A sealing order under chapter 19-03.1 seals the court record in this case. The statute is unusually strong on this point: once sealed, the court record may not be opened even by court order. 
 What it does not reach 
 static 
 The order is directed at the court record. It does not by itself change records held by other agencies, and it is not a pardon. If you need a criminal-history record corrected as well, that is a separate request to the agency that holds it. 
 This is not the general sealing chapter 
 static 
 North Dakota's general criminal-record sealing chapter, 12-60.1, uses waiting periods of three years for a misdemeanor and five for a felony, a clear-and-convincing burden, and a hearing no earlier than forty-five days after filing. None of that applies here. Chapter 19-03.1 makes sealing mandatory on motion when its own conditions are met.

nd-cover-and-contents 
 cover_and_contents 
 Your North Dakota Sealing Packet 
 custom_pleading 
 required 
 What this packet is 
 static 
 This packet asks the court that entered your judgment to seal the court record of a first-offense marijuana or THC possession case under North Dakota Century Code chapter 19-03.1. Under that chapter the court must seal the record on motion when the conditions are met, so this is a motion asking for something the statute requires rather than a request for the court's discretion. 
 What is in it 
 contents_list 
 What you still have to do 
 participant_checklist_summary 
 What this packet is not 
 static 
 This packet is not legal advice and it is not a filing service. It is prepared from the facts you gave and from the statute; you file it yourself. It does not use North Dakota's general sealing chapter 12-60.1, which has its own waiting periods and its own burden of proof, and it is not the Summary Pardon Application administered by the Pardon Advisory Board.

nd-legal-effect 
 legal_effect_explanation 
 What sealing does, and what it does not do 
 process_guidance 
 required 
 nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-legal-effect-explanation-3 
 What the order does 
 static 
 A sealing order under chapter 19-03.1 seals the court record in this case. The statute is unusually strong on this point: once sealed, the court record may not be opened even by court order. 
 What it does not reach 
 static 
 The order is directed at the court record. It does not by itself change records held by other agencies, and it is not a pardon. If you need a criminal-history record corrected as well, that is a separate request to the agency that holds it. 
 This is not the general sealing chapter 
 static 
 North Dakota's general criminal-record sealing chapter, 12-60.1, uses waiting periods of three years for a misdemeanor and five for a felony, a clear-and-convincing burden, and a hearing no earlier than forty-five days after filing. None of that applies here. Chapter 19-03.1 makes sealing mandatory on motion when its own conditions are met.

 Once the district attorney general's office prepares the petition and proposed order, the petitioner files them with the clerk of the convicting court under § 40-32-108(a) and pays the clerk's fee under T.C.A. § 8-21-401. The generated artifact on this route is the participant's own controlled written request to the office of the district attorney general, together with the participant's controlled eligibility record. It is not the statutory petition and it is not the proposed order: T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e) requires both of those to be prepared by the office of the district attorney general and given to the petitioner to be filed with the clerk. LegalEase does not draft, complete, sign or hold out either instrument as its own, and does not make the district attorney general's legal determination.
Mistaken identity is one of the § 40-32-106(a)(1) grounds, and those records must be removed and destroyed without cost to the person.

Section 40-32-106(a)(1) requires the records to be removed and destroyed without cost to the person, and the general assembly's stated intent is that no fee ever be charged where the charge was dismissed for a reason other than successful diversion completion.
No indigency or fee-waiver provision appears anywhere in the reorganized T.C.A. §§ 40-32-106 through 40-32-110. None is asserted.
No indigency or fee-waiver provision appears anywhere in the reorganized §§ 40-32-106 through 40-32-110. None is asserted.
Not applicable — no fee is charged.

After a denial 
 No further petition for at least two years from the date of the denial, under § 40-32-108(d)(3).

After a denial 
 No further petition for at least two years from the date of the denial.

Any Class C or Class D felony among the offences 
 Ten years since completion of sentence for that offence, measured at the time of filing.

Any misdemeanour or Class E felony among the offences 
 Five years since completion of sentence for that offence, measured at the time of filing.

Burglary under T.C.A. § 39-13-1002 committed on or after 2026-07-01 
 Ten years. Public Chapter 930 moved the offence from the Class E list to the Class D list for offences committed on or after 2026-07-01 only. An offence committed before that date is unaffected and the change is not applied retroactively.

Class C or Class D felony 
 Ten years from completion of the sentence, measured at the time of filing.

Court timing 
 The court may not order sooner than 61 days after service on the district attorney general.

Court timing 
 The court may not order sooner than 61 days after the petition is served on the district attorney general, who has 60 days to submit recommendations.

Every § 40-32-107(c) route 
 Fifteen years from completion of the sentence imposed for the offence being expunged, measured at the time of filing the petition. This is the longest waiting period in the chapter.

Misdemeanour or Class E felony 
 Five years from completion of the sentence, measured at the time of filing.

Pre-order clock 
 None. The 61-day pre-order clock lives in § 40-32-108(d)(1) and does not reach this section.

Recovery court 
 Successful completion of a certified recovery court programme established under title 16.

Sentence completion 
 All requirements of the sentence for the offence being expunged must be fulfilled: every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment paid, any term of imprisonment or probation completed, and all conditions of supervised or unsupervised release met.

Single criminal episode 
 Contemporaneous convictions at the same location in a single continuous episode with a single criminal intent count as one offence, so a single episode does not consume both slots.

Statutory waiting period 
 None. Section 40-32-109 states no waiting period.

Statutory waiting period 
 None. Subsection (d) states no waiting period, and none is imported from subsection (b) or (c).

TBI certificate 
 Required on this route. The § 40-32-102(c) exemption for § 40-32-106 expunctions does not apply where the expunction resulted from successful completion of diversion, so the court must obtain and attach the certificate before entering the order.

TBI transmission 
 The court sends the order to the TBI within 30 days of entry.

TBI transmission 
 The court sends the order to the TBI within 30 days of entry. Nothing changes on a background check until it arrives.

Ten-year interval 
 The offence being expunged must have occurred at least ten years after the person's conviction for an offence under T.C.A. § 55-10-401. This is an interval between two events rather than a wait from sentence completion.

Trigger 
 Receipt of a pardon by the Governor, following a positive vote of the board of parole to receive a pardon. The three requirements at (d)(1)(A), (B) and (C) are cumulative.

Trigger 
 Successful completion of the diversion programme and dismissal of the charges. There is no further waiting period, but a petition is still required and nothing happens without one.

When the clock starts 
 On completion of the entire sentence, including all fines, restitution, court costs and other assessments. Outstanding amounts mean the sentence is not complete and the clock has not started.

When the clock starts 
 On completion of the sentence, which means every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment paid, any term of imprisonment or probation completed, and all conditions of supervised or unsupervised release met. Anything outstanding means the sentence is not complete and the clock has not started.

Any case where the violence question is genuinely contested. After Public Chapter 719 it is a merits factor the court weighs, and arguing it is individualized advocacy; the participant is handed off to an attorney.
Any dispute with the district attorney general about eligibility, or any indication the office will oppose.

Eligibility is disputed by the district attorney general's office. That is a contested determination for that office and, on filing, for the court; it is handed off to an attorney rather than argued in the packet.

The district attorney general files evidence that the court does have a history of the arrest. That converts the matter into a contested question of fact and the participant is handed off to an attorney.
The district attorney general's office declines to prepare the petition, or indicates it will oppose.

The office of the district attorney general declines to prepare the petition, or indicates it will oppose. Self-help stops and the participant is handed off to an attorney; the participant keeps the generated request, the controlled factual record and the instructions.

Where the eligibility requirements are satisfied there is a rebuttable presumption that the petition should be granted, which shifts the practical burden to the district attorney general to object. Public Chapter 719, effective 2026-04-14, rewrote T.C.A. § 40-32-108(d)(2) and preserved that presumption for petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E), while providing that the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety. The packet may describe the presumption; it may not state that the petition will be granted.

Statewide in scope with county-level filing. An ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred (art. 55A.251) — not the county of residence. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

court 
 A district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, filed through the district clerk 
 No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

An ex parte petition, verified, filed with the district clerk of the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, through eFileTexas, in person, or by mail where the clerk allows. The matter is a new civil action and receives a new cause number. Justice court or municipal court of record is available under art. 55A.252 only where the arrest was for a fine-only offence.

102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100.
55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art.
Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B.
The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant.
The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).
The participant does not serve in the ordinary case; a certificate of service is included only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly.
A state or local agency with a listed e-mail address must accept electronic service.
The clerk sends the petition and notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested, or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax.

Hearing 
 None. Under art. 55A.256(d) the court enters a final order without a hearing, because the prosecutor has already verified the application upstream.

After verifying the allegations the prosecutor supplements missing arrest information, forwards the application to the district court with the agency list attached, and requests the order, and the court enters a final order without a hearing.

proposed_order: OCA Model Order of Nondisclosure under Section 411.0735
The complete list of prior convictions and deferred adjudications
The judge's signature on the proposed order
The petitioner signs the petition. The proposed order is completed except for the judge's signature.
Not required by Subchapter E-1 for the petition. County practice may differ and the packet directs the participant to ask the clerk.

Statewide in scope with court-level filing. The petition is filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, including deferred adjudication community supervision — not the county of arrest. This is the single biggest venue difference from expunction, and it matters because a person with both an expunction and a nondisclosure may be filing in two different courts.

court 
 The court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, filed through its clerk 
 Statewide mechanism with court-level filing. The OCA model petition, order and instructions are published statewide by the Office of Court Administration and county clerks across Texas republish them and refer filers to the OCA site. No county form is promoted to statewide status by this memo, and no local variant is asserted.

A petition filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, who forwards it to the court. Under Gov't Code 411.0745(a) it may be filed in person, electronically or by mail. OCA instructions state that in most courts a proposed order must be submitted with the petition. An order of nondisclosure applies to one offence, so multiple offences require multiple orders.
OCA instructions describe the total as typically about $280, varying by county, and direct the filer to call the clerk.
Read at source on 2026-08-06: the subsection sets the type of fee, not an amount, so county civil filing fee schedules govern and no flat statutory figure exists for a petition-based nondisclosure.
Under Gov't Code 411.0745(b) the petition must be accompanied by payment of a fee that generally applies to the filing of a civil case.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, on the statewide bilingual form approved by the Supreme Court of Texas in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, which the clerk must make available without charge or request.
Under Gov't Code 411.0745(e) the court provides notice to the state and an opportunity for a hearing on receipt of the petition.
Where local practice requires the filer to deliver a copy to the prosecuting attorney, the packet includes proof that the district attorney received a copy of the petition.

Any other misdemeanour 
 The second anniversary of completing the sentence.

Hearing 
 Required unless the state does not request one before the 45th day after receiving notice and the court finds entitlement and best interest of justice.

Misdemeanour punishable by fine only 
 Immediately on completion of the sentence.
The prosecutor opposes the petition or requests a hearing.

The complete list of prior convictions and deferred adjudications
The judge's signature on the proposed order
The petitioner signs the petition. The proposed order is completed except for the judge's signature.
Not required by Subchapter E-1 for the petition. County practice may differ and the packet directs the participant to ask the clerk.

Statewide in scope with court-level filing. The petition is filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, including deferred adjudication community supervision — not the county of arrest. This is the single biggest venue difference from expunction, and it matters because a person with both an expunction and a nondisclosure may be filing in two different courts.

court 
 The court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, filed through its clerk 
 Statewide mechanism with court-level filing. The OCA model petition, order and instructions are published statewide by the Office of Court Administration and county clerks across Texas republish them and refer filers to the OCA site. No county form is promoted to statewide status by this memo, and no local variant is asserted.

A petition filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, who forwards it to the court. Under Gov't Code 411.0745(a) it may be filed in person, electronically or by mail. OCA instructions state that in most courts a proposed order must be submitted with the petition. An order of nondisclosure applies to one offence, so multiple offences require multiple orders.
OCA instructions describe the total as typically about $280, varying by county, and direct the filer to call the clerk.
Read at source on 2026-08-06: the subsection sets the type of fee, not an amount, so county civil filing fee schedules govern and no flat statutory figure exists for a petition-based nondisclosure.
Under Gov't Code 411.0745(b) the petition must be accompanied by payment of a fee that generally applies to the filing of a civil case.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, on the statewide bilingual form approved by the Supreme Court of Texas in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, which the clerk must make available without charge or request.
Under Gov't Code 411.0745(e) the court provides notice to the state and an opportunity for a hearing on receipt of the petition.
Where local practice requires the filer to deliver a copy to the prosecuting attorney, the packet includes proof that the district attorney received a copy of the petition.

Felony 
 The fifth anniversary of the discharge and dismissal.

Hearing 
 Required unless the state does not request one before the 45th day after receiving notice and the court finds entitlement and best interest of justice.

Misdemeanour not within Penal Code Chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43 or 46 
 On the discharge and dismissal. No waiting period.

Misdemeanour under Penal Code Chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43 or 46 
 The second anniversary of the discharge and dismissal.
The prosecutor opposes the petition or requests a hearing.

The participant's signature and date on the motion
The participant signs the motion. The order is left unsigned for the judge or commissioner.
Not required by 77-40a-105 or by the published forms.

The court that handled the dismissed criminal case. Form 1501CR carries a district-or-justice-court election on its face, so the remedy runs in both court levels. Whether a judge or a court commissioner decides turns on the case category and the judicial district, which is why Utah Courts publishes a judge version and a commissioner version of the same motion.

court 
 The district or justice court that dismissed the criminal case 
 The participant files the motion in the court that handled the case, on the existing case rather than as a new action, and the court enters the order on form 1502CR. The order reaches only the Utah state courts' publicly searchable database; prosecuting, arresting and other agency records are untouched, and the case history remains findable by case number.
Because this is a motion in an existing criminal case rather than a new civil action, the expungement cover sheet and civil filing fee are not indicated.
The ordinary court fee waiver process applies to any fee the clerk does charge. Utah Courts publishes 1306GE, Order on Motion to Waive Fees for Criminal Expungement, in the same forms category.
On the judge track the participant files a Notice to Submit for Decision once the response time has run; on the commissioner track a Notice of Hearing is filed.
Ordinary motion service on the prosecuting attorney under the applicable rules.

Appeal window 
 No appeal may have been filed in the dismissed case within that same 30-day period.

Every 77-40a-105 route 
 At least 30 days from the day on which the case was dismissed.

Relative to automatic expungement 
 This remedy runs on a 30-day clock, against the 180 days a dismissal with prejudice waits for automatic expungement under 77-40a-206. It is the faster interim step, not a replacement.

entries: The statement that none of the RCW 9.97.010(1)(c) bars applies

A qualified court, and RCW 9.97.010(2) closes the set: a Washington superior court in the county where the applicant resides, or the superior court of the county that sentenced or adjudicated them. Where the sentencing or adjudicating court was a court of limited jurisdiction, the qualified court is the superior court of that county of conviction or adjudication; the district or municipal court that convicted the applicant is never itself a qualified court. Because the set is closed and statutory, one statewide packet serves the whole state as to venue and the county is a participant answer rather than a routing branch. The packet routes to the superior court of the county of the applicant's conviction or adjudication, because RCW 9.97.020(8) provides that court may not decline to consider the application.

court 
 The superior court of a qualified county under RCW 9.97.010(2) 
 Filed as a civil action under RCW 9.97.020(7), at the superior court clerk's office of the chosen qualified county, with the notice to each prosecuting attorney RCW 9.97.020(6) requires. The packet routes to the superior court of the county of conviction or adjudication because RCW 9.97.020(8) provides that it may not decline to consider the application. The superior court of the county where the applicant resides remains statutorily available and may be nearer, and a participant who prefers it may use it, but that court may decline to consider the application; if it does, it must dismiss without prejudice, must state the reason on the order, and the applicant may refile in another qualified court. There is no statutory transfer procedure: the remedy is refiling by the applicant, not transfer by the court. Confirming intake with the clerk is prudent practice and not a legal prerequisite, and it is not a condition of generating this packet; which counties require additional accompanying documents under local superior court rules is a separate open filing-instruction question.
A superior court civil filing fee applies.

The Administrative Office of the Courts' own instructions confirm that there is a filing fee and that a participant who cannot pay may ask for a waiver; they do not state the amount and none is asserted here, so the packet does not quote a figure and directs the participant to the clerk for it.
A participant who cannot afford the filing fee may ask the court for a waiver by GR 34 motion, which is the route the Administrative Office of the Courts' instructions name.
